newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 12 pct.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in January is estimated to have fallen by up to 12 percent from December, plantation houses said on Wednesday.
"The fall was expected as it is still the seasonal downward period and January was a low production month," a trader said.
"There was also a drought particularly in the main growing areas of Johor and Pahang," he said.

The trader added that production in February could record a larger drop due to the festivals of Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr, which limited harvesting. Some traders estimated the Febraury decline at between 15 and 20 percent.
Private crop forecaster Ivan Wong had estimated January output at 568,000 tonnes.
Traders has estimated end-January stocks at 710,000-750,000 tonnes against end-December's 792,607 tonnes.
Exports in January were estimated at 545,000-555,000 tonnes against PORLA's 637,899 tonnes in December.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is due to release official January crop data on February 22.
